record.original_question: The existence of one hyperbolic prime closed geodesic on a Finsler S^2 implies the existence of infinitely many distinct prime closed geodesics.

evidence.quote: The existence of one hyperbolic prime closed geodesic on a Finsler S^2 implies the existence of infinitely many distinct prime closed geodesics.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a Finsler metric on the 2-sphere $S^2$, i.e. a continuous function $F: TS^2 \to [0,\infty)$ that is smooth and positive on $TS^2 \setminus \{0\}$, positively homogeneous of degree one in the fiber variable, and whose vertical Hessian $\tfrac{1}{2}\partial^2(F^2)/\partial y^i \partial y^j$ is positive definite on $TS^2 \setminus \{0\}$. A closed geodesic is called prime if it is not an iterate of a shorter closed geodesic. The linearized Poincaré return map of a prime closed geodesic on a Finsler $S^2$ is a symplectic $2\times 2$ matrix; the geodesic is called hyperbolic if this map has two real eigenvalues different from $\pm 1$.

Prove or disprove: every Finsler 2-sphere $(S^2, F)$ that admits at least one hyperbolic prime closed geodesic admits infinitely many geometrically distinct prime closed geodesics.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2023 result establishes that every Finsler metric on $S^2$ with at least one prime closed geodesic that is not irrationally elliptic admits infinitely many geometrically distinct prime closed geodesics. Since hyperbolic closed geodesics are not irrationally elliptic, this confirms the conjecture (a "two-or-infinity" type theorem for Finsler $S^2$, related to and extending the Hofer–Wysocki–Zehnder conjecture).

status_evidence.title: Proof of Hofer-Wysocki-Zehnder's two or infinity conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: a Finsler metric on S^2 with at least one closed geodesic that is not irrationally elliptic must have infinitely many prime closed geodesics
status_evidence.claim: Hyperbolic closed geodesics are not irrationally elliptic, so this implies Long's conjecture in the stated form.

status_evidence.title: On the minimal number of closed geodesics on positively curved Finsler spheres
status_evidence.snippet: Recent works establish two-or-infinity dichotomies for closed geodesics on Finsler 2-spheres.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms widespread acceptance of the resolution of the hyperbolic-implies-infinity statement on Finsler $S^2$.
